subject: Discovery recap — integration & POC plan (FastRetail)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — integration & POC plan (FastRetail)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the context on search latency and the reranking challenges. Quick recap from our side and the proposed POC/onboarding plan so we’re aligned on goals and owners.

Pain points you shared
- Slow and inconsistent product search results during peak windows (spikes in latency, poor 95th pctl).
- High unit cost for your current reranking model inference.
- Fragmented stack: Elasticsearch for retrieval + a homegrown reranker that’s expensive to operate and hard to scale.

Current stack we heard
- Retrieval: Elasticsearch (self-managed on AWS)
- Reranker: internal model served via Java microservice (K8s)
- Primary languages: Python for data pipelines, Java for serving layer

Success criteria (what FastRetail wants to validate in the POC)
- Maintain or improve relevance vs. current reranker (quant metrics + sample golden set).
- 95th percentile latency under 500ms for product-recommendation flows and under 200ms for autocomplete use-cases.
- Reduce inference unit cost by ~30-40% or show a clear path via batching/quantization.

Proposed 4-week POC plan (attached: FastRetail-POC-Plan-20260714.pdf)
- Week 1: Integration — SDK install, sample dataset ingestion, baseline metrics collection.
- Week 2: Model & routing configuration — embeddings + rerank pipeline; quick A/B against current reranker.
- Week 3: Tuning & load testing — latency/throughput tuning, caching config, sample SLO tests.
- Week 4: Evaluation & next-steps — results review, proposal for Dedicated/Private if needed, draft SOW.

Owners / leads
- Redwood: Ben Carter (AE) — commercial lead; Marissa Cole (Solutions) — solution architecture & evals; Vanessa Ortiz (CS) — onboarding and SSO/KMS ops.
- FastRetail: Alex Johnson (Eng lead) — integration owner; Priya Reddy (PM) — success criteria & exec sponsor.

Open questions / asks for FastRetail
1) Confirm primary SDK preference: Python for data pipelines and Java for serving — we can prioritize samples for both.
2) Provide a small representative dataset (anonymized) and a golden relevance set if available.
3) Expected QPS and peak concurrency we should test against.
4) Any security constraints (SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM) for the PoC environment.

Next steps
- I’ll send calendar options for a 30-45m technical kickoff (proposed: Mon Jul 19, 10:00 AM PT). Please confirm availability.
- We’ll upload the POC plan and a brief SOW draft to the shared Drive once we close scope.

Attachments: FastRetail-POC-Plan-20260714.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0143

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — integration & POC plan (FastRetail)

Thanks Ben — this looks great and matches how we saw the call. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- SDK preference: Python for data pipelines is ideal; our serving stack is Java/K8s — Java client or a lightweight REST integration would work there.
- Security: we are interested in Private or Dedicated options long-term, but for the POC can we start with hosted endpoints with strict VPC egress rules and logs retained per our policy? We can share the security checklist after the kickoff.
- QPS: baseline is ~50 qps across two regions, peaks up to 250 qps in promotions.

We can make the proposed Mon Jul 19 10:00 AM PT work. I’ll loop in our solution architect (Samira Khan) on the invite.

Alex

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — integration & POC plan (FastRetail)

Alex / Priya — great, thanks for the fast reply and for the QPS details. Couple of quick notes: 

- SDKs & API compatibility: Redwood provides first-class Python and Node SDKs, plus a Java SDK (beta) and a simple REST/gRPC API that integrates with existing Java services. For your serving layer we can provide a small Java example and a standalone REST wrapper to deploy in your K8s.
- Hosted POC: we can start on hosted endpoints with strict network controls / VPC peering and logs retention configured to your policy. If after the POC you want Dedicated or Private we’ll include a cost estimate in the SOW.
- We’ll include Samira in the kickoff invite — thanks for adding her.

I uploaded the POC plan and a draft SOW to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h/view (SOW-Draft-FastRetail-20260715.docx attached here as well). I’ll also add the HubSpot record for this opportunity: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/7654321

Confirming meeting: Mon Jul 19, 10:00 AM PT — I’ll send the calendar invite with a short agenda (kickoff, integration owners, security checklist, immediate next steps).

Marissa will lead the technical presales intro and Vanessa will be your onboarding contact for access/SSO details.

Action items assigned:
- FastRetail: share anonymized sample dataset + golden set (Alex / Priya)
- Redwood: calendar invite + pre-kickoff checklist (Ben / Marissa / Vanessa)

Thanks — talk soon.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@fastretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — integration & POC plan (FastRetail)

Hi Alex / Priya — quick onboarding checklist from the CS side to keep the POC moving smoothly: 

1) Access: please provide a dev AWS account (IAM role) or a space where we can run small-scale load tests. If you prefer hosted endpoints for the POC, share any IP allowlists or VPC peering contacts.
2) Dataset: anonymized sample (10k-50k items) + golden relevance set (10-50 queries) so we can compute baselines.
3) Security: SAML SSO contact + any KMS restrictions. If you want KMS-backed keys, we’ll coordinate with security; otherwise we can use Redwood-managed keys for the POC.
4) Expected traffic patterns: confirm 50 qps baseline / 250 qps peaks (per Ben/Alex thread).
5) Integration point: please identify a single Java service owner who can accept the REST wrapper (Samira?); we’ll provide a Java example for sidecar or direct client usage.

I’ll follow up with a short pre-kickoff checklist doc and the calendar invite. If there are any procurement approvals needed for extended Dedicated trials, flag them now so we can involve Legal.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
